references.notes: 82-5-22 (mainly BM 54061-55432). Eleven cases. One from Assyria (1882 P 1259), in Bezold’s catalogue; two from the Babylon overseer, sent to Baghdad on 31 December 1881 and 12 February 1882 (dispatch inventory 1882 P 3013, cases nos. 9-10); eight from the Abu Habbah overseer (dispatch inventory 1882 P 2766, cases nos. 9-16). Sent from Baghdad on 25 February 1882 (Trustees’ Minutes, 22 April 1882). A note by Pinches (WAA Corr. 1882) confirms the dates of receipt of this and the remaining large Rassam consignments, which were no longer reported to the Trustees in any systematic way. Unless Dailem was still being worked (see section on excavations), this consignment should only have had material from Kuyunjik, Babylon itself, and Abu Habbah. Some of the last are marked A.H., and the registrar relied on this; the provenance “Babylon,” assigned to some pieces marked A.H. in the range 82-5-22, 377-390 (BM 54226-54239), results from dittography. It is unclear how the registrar decided that particular pieces came from Babylon. A lone “Dailem” near the end, 82-5- 22, 1760 (BM 55427), was evidently generated by the presence, in the text, of a personal name incorporating the place-name Dilbat. A tablet that is probably 82-5-22, 356 (BM 91081), is very plausibly assigned to Borsippa in the 1884 Return, 26. In fact Rassam bought it as from Babylon (letter to Pinches, 9 June 1882). Another likely Borsippa piece is 82-5-22, 1048 (BM 93014), which is registered as “Kuyunjik(?).” Many 82-5-22 Nabonidus cylinder fragments join 96-4-9, 513 (BM 22408), a fragment bought from Daud Thoma.
